rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes helium-ion irradiation, whereas the paper studied an as-cast WTaTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy compared with pure tungsten; these are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-vacuum helium irradiation at 500°C, while the paper used room-temperature compression, indentation plastometry from 25–500°C in air, and scratch testing; the conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes helium-vacancy clusters enhancing dislocation glide, whereas the paper attributes strength to solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion, and plasticity to Ti, V, Zr effects on dislocation cores and grain-boundary cohesion; these are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased high-temperature plastic strain and toughness from irradiation, while the paper reports higher strength, plasticity, and toughness in the HEA relative to tungsten without irradiation; the property direction is similar but the cause and context are unrelated.
